research_concepts: PNR fail as a defensive-suppression outcome
PULL_UP shot as a candidate counter
play-type lift relative to a baseline
consistency of counter effects across defensive units
methodological_questions: What is the baseline against which PULL_UP lift after PNR fail is measured?
What defines a unit (team-season, lineup, or matchup), and how many units exist?
Is the criterion of lift > 0 in at least 70% of units with median lift > 2pp a pre-specifiable and interpretable test?
How are PNR fail and PULL_UP possessions identified, and are those labels free of outcome leakage?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned no records, so no earlier study by this project on PNR-fail-to-PULL_UP counters, unit-level lift consistency, or median-lift thresholds is available in this setting.
No prior result for this question, including any supported, rejected, or inconclusive status, can be cited.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP is a league-wide counter to failed PNR possessions.
Whether the proposed 70% and 2pp thresholds are appropriate, or how they were chosen.
Whether any unit definition, baseline, or sample size has been tested before.
own_inferences: The question as posed is underspecified: 'unit' and 'lift' are not defined, so the test cannot be run as written.
The data description supports the inputs needed (play-by-play action type and sub-type, shot distance and result, points, defensive matchups), so a team-season defensive test is plausibly feasible.
Per-unit PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP sequences are probably sparse for many teams in a single season, which would make unit-level sign counts noisy.
The 2025-26 regular season was complete by 2026-04-13, before the question date of 2026-05-23, so it can be used. The 2025-26 playoffs were partial on that date and should be excluded.
uncertainties: Unit definition (team, lineup, or matchup) and its count are unknown.
Baseline for lift (league PULL_UP rate, other actions after PNR fail, or the same unit's non-PNR possessions) is unspecified.
Exact derivation of 'PNR fail' (points-based, turnover-based, or shot-quality-based) is not given, and a points-based definition risks outcome-derived labels.
Whether the derived play-type graph records are validated against raw play-by-play is unknown.
Stability of play-type coding across 2022-23 to 2025-26 is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so retrieved history did not alter the decision. The decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone: the question is testable only after the unit, baseline, and PNR-fail definitions are fixed, so the decision is to proceed with changes.

blocking_constraints.text: Lift is not defined for a unit with few PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP possessions, so unit-level estimates may be unstable without a shrinkage or minimum-count rule.
Per-unit exposure to PNR fail followed by PULL_UP may be too small in a single season to support a sign test on 70% of units.
If PNR fail is defined by the possession's points, the label is partly determined by the outcome being tested.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so whether this question has been answered is unknown. Nothing is cited.

risks.text: Sign-count thresholds (70% of units with lift > 0) and a median-lift threshold of 2pp need enough units and possessions to distinguish a true effect from noise; power is not computed.
PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP sequences per unit-season may be rare, so many units could have unstable or undefined lift.
Single-season unit lift estimates are noisy; without split-half or cross-season reliability checks, sign consistency may reflect noise.
If units are chosen because they show large PNR-fail counts or extreme lift, selection will inflate apparent lift.
Defining PNR fail by points scored makes the counter label depend on the outcome measured by lift.
Possession-level features built from later events (for example the final shot type) could leak outcome information into the PNR-fail or PULL_UP label.
PULL_UP frequency and efficiency differ by league context and season; a fixed 2pp threshold may not be comparable across seasons or baselines.
Shot quality, shooter identity, defender matchup, score margin, clock, and period may drive both PULL_UP selection and efficiency after a PNR fail.
Play-type labels from play-by-play action and sub-type fields, and the graph-derived possession records, may misclassify PNR fail or PULL_UP possessions.
Testing several counters, unit definitions, or thresholds and reporting the one that passes inflates false-positive rates.
Without placebo actions (other actions after PNR fail), a positive lift may reflect general offensive context rather than a counter.
Rule changes and style shifts across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can change PULL_UP frequency and efficiency, so pooling seasons may mix regimes.
Joins between play-by-play, rotation intervals, and the graph-derived possession records may misalign possessions or double-count units.

design.estimand: Within each defensive unit, the difference in expected points per possession between possessions where the offense takes a PULL_UP shot after a failed PNR and comparable possessions where it does not (or takes a different action after PNR fail), with a pre-specified baseline. The primary criterion is the share of units with positive lift and the median lift.
design.unit: Defensive team-season (30 teams × completed seasons). Lineup-level units are a secondary analysis only if each has enough PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP possessions. The unit definition must be fixed before analysis.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (the 2025-26 regular season was complete by 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs, which were partial on 2026-05-23. Playoffs analysed separately if at all. PNR fail defined a priori from a non-outcome-based rule (for example, a ball-handler screen-and-roll ending in a non-shot-attempt or a defensive-recovery event) rather than points scored.
design.power: Not computed. Before analysis, simulate unit-level sign counts and median lift under plausible effect sizes (for example 1-3pp) with observed per-unit exposure, and require adequate power for the 70% and 2pp criteria. If power is inadequate, report the test as inconclusive rather than rejected.
design.controls: Adjust for shot distance and shot zone, shooter identity or shooter-quality proxy, defender matchup minutes, score margin, period, and clock. Use a regression with unit fixed effects, and report unadjusted and adjusted lift.
design.falsification: Placebo counters: compare PULL_UP lift after PNR fail with lift of other actions after PNR fail, and with PULL_UP lift after non-PNR possessions. Also test a pre-period placebo window. A positive result that also appears in placebo comparisons should be treated as an artifact.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary test (share of units with lift > 0 at ≥70%, median lift > 2pp). Other unit definitions, thresholds, and seasons are secondary and reported with correction (e.g., Holm) or labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) at least 70% of units (≥21 of 30 team-seasons, or the pre-specified equivalent) have positive adjusted lift, (b) the median adjusted lift exceeds 2pp, (c) the bootstrap 95% CI for the median excludes 2pp below, and (d) the effect is not matched by the placebo counters. Rejected if the adequately powered test fails (a) or (b). Untestable or uncertain if power is insufficient or labels fail validation.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (2025-26 complete as of 2026-04-13); graph-derived play-type possession records built from the same play-by-play with a version hash recorded; 2025-26 playoffs excluded as partial on 2026-05-23.

methodological_questions: Does PULL_UP lift over baseline exceed 0 in at least 70% of units?
Is median lift above 2 percentage points after PNR fail?
How should counter-strategy lift be measured across units with sparse exposure?
args.query: Historical evidence on whether PULL_UP shooting is a league-wide counter to failed pick-and-roll (PNR) possessions, including unit-level lift consistency and median lift thresholds

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
